The pair I just ordered (no sole, Thunderbird beadwork) have a problem: the cushioned pad inside the moc is simply TOO narrow on the left moc. As a result, my left pinkie toe falls off that pad and seems to rub against the edge of the pad. After about 2 days of wearing these around the house, my pinkie was SO SORE that I couldn't even wear normal shoes without being in pain. I didn't get a blister (luckily!), but geez, that pinkie toe was really rubbed painfully. Since I'd worn these in at a hotel and VRBO (but never outside, as they have no rubber sole), they were stained on the bottom. I couldn't return them in

They are ungodly comfortable and I hate to take them off, hate that it is winter and I can't wear them all the time! We have had a few warmer days here in the South this winter and I have worn them to run errands and of course just around the house. Since they are soft soled I don't want to shred them by walking on the city sidewalks which is a shame; I walk dogs for a living and treasure a good pair of walking shoes. title: If anything these might be a bit small--maybe I'm between 9.5 and 9.75, but the 10s are perfect--not too big for sure!
text: I'm a 9.5 in Lowa and a few other brands, but in Merrell's the 10s feel GREAT! These are great shoes with good traction and stability. I think the sole should be like 20% stiffer and heel raised 15-20% higher (for more back support). I definitely feel a bit more of the rocks and stuff through these--but it's not like they're made for super heavy duty. I'll update once I know how the MESH holds up (I wore them without socks in a light rain with very shallow puddles yesterday just to see how they did--I'm sure the mesh would let in water, but they kept my feet dry in the light rain for a 15 minute walk). So far, they're comfortable enough to sleep in with no break in which is what I've come to expect from Merrell (these are my 3rd pair in about 9 years--with one or two pairs of Lowas in there as well). BUT I wear one pair of shoes for 99% of the time--I don't change shoes for work or play or hiking or walks (so after 2-3 years, they start feeling like they're bottoming out and have less bounce).

My toes do touch sometimes, but the toe box is generous and they're not uncomfortable. Unfortunately, neither size seems to fit me great, so I had to choose and the 11.5D just seemed far too large with the Ventilator. For the record, I don't think my feet could fall in between sizes more then they do with this shoe, and I don't know why it happens, because they're very spacious. Overall, it's a great shoe and I really love it, but just wish the sizing was better for me. Update: Well, several months later and I wish I had gone with the larger size. Never felt that my feet were too hot when paired with merino wool socks. Good grip overall on dry surfaces and fairly easy to keep clean Comfortable fit but not too tight based on your shoe size. I went with the Wide option in the shoe which allows more room for your toes. They were comfortable from the very beginning so didn't require a break in period. Quality materials on the shoe. title: Not the best for wide feet
text: The Dansko Pro XP has really helped reduce the amount of back and knee pain I feel after working a twelve hour shift at the hospital. I feel like theses shoes impove my overall posture. However, I don't like how narrow these shoes are. I have wide feet, as do many other people. Dansko Wide Pro XP shoes are hard to come by and these shoes take me a long time to break in because they hurt my wide feet after a few short hours. I also don't think they last as long for people with wide feet. Every pair of Dansko shoes that I have owned start to crack on the top and side of the shoe after a year or so. Considering the price of these shoes, I would expect them to last a lot longer than a year. These shoes always last longer for my friends with narrow feet.

I will say that I had tried the Pro XP and the Professional (previous generation, firmer inside the shoe, no memory foam), and thought the Professional felt better but decided I should go with the memory foam insole. title: Breeze-3 great, Breeze-2 not...
text: I've been wearing Merrill Encore Breeze clogs for several years and love them. I especially like how the toe-box is roomy yet the uppers keep the clogs on without flopping or twisting. So, you get both comfort and support - a rarity in clogs, IMHO. BUT there's a catch... Inconsistency. After reading reviews of the Breeze-2 & 3 it was evident that the snug, supportive fit had been changed in favor of a wider cut that slips around and flops. The complaints seemed to be about the 3's, which I presumed to be the newer model (I don't recall my older pairs even having a number). Anyway, I ordered a pair of EACH due to color availability. To my surprise, the Breeze-3's fit perfectly and it's the 2's that are too wide and flop! I don't know if it's a fluke or what, but the 3's are 5-stars for me, and the 2's are going to have to go back. My suggestion is to try a pair of each because, as I said, it is the opposite of what I expected. Good luck.

The arch support is now placed too close to my heel to be of any use for supporting my aging foot. This shoe now feels cheaply made without substance and, frankly, it is too expensive for what you get. Merrell, if you are seeing this, please bring back the old style used for years. title: A great every-day shoe for problem feet.

Plus, with age, the balls of my feet have become increasingly achy, and thinner soled shoes no longer work for me (I need a certain amount of cushioning). I normally wear either a 9 or 9 1/2 wide in most shoes. Skechers size 9 fits me perfectly. To add even more cushioning to the ball of the foot (which is nice, but not necessary with these shoes); and mostly to provide a minimum of arch support, I've inserted Profoot 2oz. Miracle Custom Molding Insoles into these shoes, and they do the trick nicely. I usually have to wear the shoes a couple of times, first, to compress them so that there's room for the inserts. Not a big deal.

text: I bought these shoes hoping to have a summer sandal that wasn't a thong. I read quite a number of the reviews, and even though many of them complained about the shoe (the foot being pushed onto the outside), I figured these people possibly weren't used to wearing shoes with built-in support. (I, myself, wear orthotics in my shoes, but you can't wear them easily with sandals.) However, upon trying this shoe on and walking around a bit, the structured and ungiving arch actually caused sharp pain. For this type of shoe to be successful, my own opinion is that the arch needs to be slightly flexible. Since there is nothing other than two straps holding the foot in place, it becomes hard to balance on the shoe. I have normal arches although I have been experiencing plantar fasciitis which is why I wanted a shoe with more arch support, but these feel too unstable to me. Too bad, as they are good looking and I would have loved to be able to wear them all summer. (I had no complaint about the footbed; I rather enjoy letting my toes spread out as they need to. I did order a size 8 for my 8.5 size foot, and the fit was perfect.)

I had been looking for a few months at different styles as the old ones had a raised stitched line around the toe box. This was the weak point couple with the fact that they were not made of leather, but a man-made substitute. In my new pair I was looking for a smooth stitching around the toe box and they had to be made of true leather. This Segment style fit that description perfectly. I ordered the same size as my previous at 9 1/2 standard width and they fit great. They are fairly easy to slip on, with the exception of the left heel area where the top of the shoe back tries to roll inside. However, I think after wearing them a few more times this will no longer be and issue as I have only had them for 6 days so far. Overall they are very comfortable to wear and I have worn them for short periods as well as all day long so far. I would recommend them if you want a comfortable leather style slip-on loafer, definitely.

text: I do like Sketchers but finally realized that with most big companies, they produce for the "masses" and not the individual. Shoes are about as individual as they get, however, like fingerprints. I have a wide foot ACROSS THE FRONT of my foot, but a very narrow heel. Buy a wide shoe, get a wide heel, buy a narrow shoe, get a narrow heel. What the heck am I supposed to do? Oh, yeah, I just did it. Bought ortho shoes that are a bit more expensive but made for people with "real" feet - no more trying to stick heel pads in a wide shoe to keep my narrow heel from popping out as I walk, no more pain across the width of my foot from trying to stuff my foot into a narrow shoe so my heel stays in. I will say that while these Sketchers are the ultimate in comfort, they (both women's and men's) break down within 6 months or so with fairly regular wear, so we keep a few pairs on hand and recycle the old ones. The older we get, the more important comfort is and these really work. I do recommend that if you have not tried a pair on in person, it is a good idea to do so. title: Vionic Rest Bella Toe Post Sandals Work for My Problematic Feet
text: I have the Vionic Rest Bella Toe Post sandals in two different colors. I can wear these sandals despite my foot issues. I have Morton's Neuroma, a Taylor's Bunion, Neuropathy on bottoms of my feet and one weak ankle. I also have Pudendal Nerve Entrapment which can flare up with wearing the wrong shoes. My Morton's Neuroma is painless without using a metatarsal pad, my Taylor's Bunion is happy with the open style, and my general neuropathy is held at bay with the comfortable foot bed, and my ankle seems find in the Bella Toe Post Sandals. Also I don't have concerns with wearing these and creating a Pudendal Nerve flare which generally occurs in a shoe or sandals with too much arch support. I've tried other Vionics and they don't work form me because they are too wide. This style comes in a narrow width which fits my foot perfectly. I typically wear a size 8 in sneakers, and the 7 Narrow is the size for me in this style so I would say they run a little large. Both of these shoes were put into immediate service after they arrived at the house, and I’ve pretty much been wearing them every single work day for the past 3 weeks. I recently got into a health craze, and seeing that I live approximately 2 miles (each way) from work, I figured I could begin walking or biking in. The first couple days I made the trek wearing my work boots, and quickly discovered that while they might be comfortable to wear under normal circumstances, they quickly lose said comfort a mile into lengthy walk. title: A $40 shoe for $50
text: My shoe of preference for 30 years has been Asics. But over the past decade I have seen this brand bridge into a wide spectrum of shoes that no longer respects the roots that made them successful. Asics (like many competitors) have a wide range of bad cheaper shoes, to over priced higher end kicks. This "trail shoe" feels like the Blur 33s I mistakenly purchased a few years back with heavier treads. They have a soft cutiony ride, but over a few weeks of breaking in, feel like they could slip off my feet given the terrain got muddy. And they are heavy shoes as well. I feel confident on flat trails, but on a rapid decline where grip is key, I don't trust them as much as other brands. That, and the looser fit that has occurred since breaking them in had my toes banging the front of the toe box on steep downhills. I would wear these for the mild beaten sort of trail that loops around a reservoir, but won't be wearing them for the Ragnar Trail race I have in a few months. In a market with so many more serious running brands, it looks like my 3 decade relationship to Asics is coming to an end.

They're the only flip flop I can wear because I have rheumatoid arthritis in my feet pretty bad. I've had 9 metatarsal stress fractures due to walking long distances. This year I asked my husband for a new pair for my May 1st birthday. By the time he got around to it, all were sold out here on Amazon. So I choose the Reef Fanning instead as an alternate. I have to say, while they're a good shoe, they're not nearly as comfortable as the Slap 3. So in that sense, I am disappointed as I need soft cushion but support as well. I can wear the Slap 3 all day without any fractures. So this will be a test wearing the Fanning instead. PLEASE don't stop making the Slap 3 because I really depend on them to keep me mobile! Thanks!

We chose these shoes in a Men's 8 for my son, who is wears size 7 New Balance sneakers. While we thought they looked fine on his feet, he felt they were too small due to the width mid-foot; they were much more snug than what he is used to when wearing Crocs. title: PERFECT flip-flops for narrow feet
text: if you have narrow feet, these are for you! i've had other pairs of Fit-flops that didn't fit, but i wore them anyway because of the awesome soles. then i put these on... it's like they were MADE for me! love the soft fabric, and of course the sole is super comfy and supportive.

title: Comfort
text: A little on the heavy side for flip flops but extremely supportive and comfortable. Would have no problems wearing all day.

title: Most comfortable flip flop out there
text: People might be taken aback by the price on these flip flops, but believe me, they are worth it. Extremely durable, and extremely comfortable. I have had 2 back surgeries and walk my dogs 3-4 miles a day and need a good shock absorber, and these do the trick. They are also well made and last forever.

title: Good quality, good support
text: These work well for house shoes, as I can no longer be barefoot and am not a fan of slippers since I need arch support and in Florida. These are firm enough, and fit well enough, to not be a trip hazard at all. The only thing I would change is to make the foot bed, esp the heal, softer.

title: These are my most favorite and comfortable out of all of the many fit flops I have worn!
text: I love these fit flops. I have another pair identical to this that finally kicked the bucket after over five years of almost constant use. they are so comfortable I wear them in my house all day long since I have bad knees and lots of tile. I live in Arizona so I basically can wear sandals every day :-)

title: Uncomfortable.
text: I have many pair of fit flops and have never experienced an uncomfortable pair til this one. The material cut into my toe and I can’t wear them.

title: Like walking on a block of wood
text: I've owned many Fit Flops in the past and they were so comfortable, but the sole is not soft and spongy like it was before. It used to be like walking on a cloud, but now it's like walking on a block of wood. Sending it right back. Also the words Fit Flop is etched so deep on the top of the insole where the heel is that it has sharp edges and pokes my heel, probably because the sole is so hard. Maybe these are knock offs. They should never have passed quality control.

title: Bought them again
text: I had a pair for several years and bought the identical one over again. Can’t live without.

title: Terrific

title: Exactly what I wanted

title: exactly what I wanted

title: Great comfy shoe

Not sure I should do this often. They are very comfortable and I'm not so quick to say this. I often get compliments on them also. Nice comfy cute shoe if you like the round toe look, which I do. The black trim is a pretty added design touch.

title: Comfy!
text: Very comfortable. I needed a pair of simple black shoes that comfortably accommodated my arthritic feet.

title: Otherwise pretty comfortable.

text: I love these shoes!!!. Have brown and now Black. will be checking for more colors. They feel better then barefoot.!!!!!

They are still adorable and I am confident they would be as comfortable as my others if the length was correct and true to size. Because the size issue seems to be related to manufacturing, I deducted a star.

title: Comfortable shoe
text: So comfortable! They rub the back of my heels a little bit, but hopefully should be fine once they are broken in. Like walking on mini pillows.

title: The 10 was too large so I exchanged them for the 9-1/2 which seems to be good. Because I have a bad back

Because I have a bad back, I probably would not do a lot of walking in them as they don't provide the support I am used to. However, they are comfortable and easy to wear.

title: Comfortable sole. Love the shoes but I have to

title: You should buy these!

title: Very poor quality. Buyer beware!

title: Finally A Comfortable Shoe for my Neuropathy
text: I have perifial neuropathy in both feet from chemo therapy over almost 10 yrs ago. I had R TKR surgery a yr ago and two R foot surgeries 6 months ago tarsel tunnel release & Gastric Calf Stretch calf tendon cut in half. Since my TKR I can not find a comfortable shoe to wear sucks not being able to find a comfortable shoe. I have a very unique unusal foot my Ortodontic foot surg told me. I am a size 5 wide foot very high instep with high arches with large foot veins. Since my surgery my vein in my foot has shrunk some what. This shoe is so comfotable to walk in but a little tight across the top of my foot. I am hoping it will give a little as I break them in. I could not believe how comfortable they are. Like walking on a cloud. I will buy again in different colors. Thanks for these shoes. I was giving up hope in finding a shoe to walk in with our pain and discomfort. You will never know how hard your life is until you canot walk in comfort in a shoe. I gave it a 4 🌟 because of the tight fit across the top of my foot They stop are by far re most comfortable shoe I purchased and I purchased plenty only to have them colect dust collect dust. 😂

title: I love Clark's shoes
text: I love Clark's shoes. Rarely are there issues or problems with the fit. These are very comfortable and relatively easy to slip on and off. They have good support as well and a nice, cushy insole. I like them!

title: Most comforable shoes I've had
text: These are absolutely the most soft and comfortable shoes I've ever had. I have metatarsalgia (pain in the bottom front bones of the foot), and these shoes are the only ones that actually feel good on my feet. I thought my carpet was soft, but these put it to shame. I bought them my regular size, which fits my feet a bit loose, and they fit exactly like all my other shoes.

title: Wonderful shoe - just like a cloud !
text: I got 1/2 size larger due to the snug fit at my normal size. I love this shoe - I got the same pair about 3-4 years ago and so now I have an extra pair when my old pair wears out.

But the Clark Cloud Walkers feel so good on my feet. Thinking of purchasing another pair in brown. Highly recommend these especially if you're a walker like me.

title: Cushy, comfy.

title: Clarks Missed the Size Mark on this Shoe
text: I bought this shoe in my regular size, 71/2 W, a while back. I found that they were quite snug and could not be worn with any kind of sock. When I decided to order the shoe again because it's really a pretty shoe and comfortable too, I sized up to an 8W. The shoe is still snug! Clarks are my go-to shoe brand. I must have had at least a dozen pairs over the last few years. This Sillian Jetay Flat, although comfy and lightweight, does not follow the sizing I am used to. I guess I'll return this pair for an 8 1/2 W shoe. Wish me luck!

title: Comfortable but clunky

They also have no flex or softness to them. The only perk is yeah, they don't hurt my feet.. but I feel like I can't climb stairs or walk fast in these.

text: This is a BEAUTIFUL shoe but it didn't fit right on my feet and I'm sorry to say, they were like walking on a pair of Bricks!! I returned them and was quickly refunded the money for my purchase.

title: great long wearing shoes
text: I like these shoes better than there cousins dansko. They are much more comfortable, I am able to stand 8 hrs a day in them. No shoe is perfect but these come pretty close.

title: Great shoe overall; minor issues with fit
text: My clogs arrived fairly promptly, and I love how neat and stylish they look. The fit at the heel is a bit wide, but I sense that if I were to get the clogs a size down, they would not fit at the toe portion. The problem is ameliorated mostly by wearing thick socks. They're certainly not loose enough that they fall off my feet when I walk, but they are much roomier than usual shoes. For those of you with narrow feet, definitely get the lower portion of the size range you typically wear. I teach for a few hours each day and they're great! Since I'm on my feet most of the day, these clogs were a good investment. Overall, I recommend the shoe, just be cautious with the size. EDIT: Still very happy with my Sanitas, but after a couple months, I noticed that the color come off a bit onto your light-colored socks! Not sure if it's just the black-colored ones (like mine), but be wary about wearing them with white socks...

title: Burgundy size 38
text: Love these! I bought the burgundy color. I usually wear a 7.5-8 and I bought a 38 and they fit perfectly.

title: Nice!

Highly recommended.

title: I normally wear a woman's nike size 8 and bought ...

title: Smaller fit than Dansko
text: I previously wore the Dansko Professional Clog and needed a new pair. These are the same size, but definitely more narrow. They also cause a blister on the top of one of my toes. :( other than the fit issue they seem pretty much the same.

title: Odd fit...
text: I usually wear Danskos, but after reading the reviews about people swearing by Santias instead, I decided to give these a go. The color is GORGEOUS. The ones I got are a rich mahogany color with a demi-matte finish. They're not glossy. As far as fit goes, they're a little off for me. They are definitely narrow and grow within the day with warmth and friction as you move in them. With that being said, they are smaller, tighter, and painful to wear in the morning because they shrink back to originally size. After about an hour or two of walking in them, they expand normally and are comfortable. Very odd. My Danskos shaped to my foot and stayed that way. Maybe this helps Sanitas last longer? Who knows. I generally avoid wearing these during long days because they do hurt in the morning before you can warm and stretch them out.

title: Just how I like it.. my go too shoes for work.
text: I received my shoes way before I expected it. Which is perfect because I will be able to wear it next week, when I go back to work. Love these shoes, fits just how I like and great support.

title: Too small
text: Beautiful shoe but right big toe rubs and does not in my other sanita shoes. I will try a size up then star review.

title: Thanks for the Review!
text: Found out from an Amazon review that Dansko is now made in China, but that Sanita was the original Danish maker. Ordered a pair, which are nearly exact to my old Dansko clogs...fit is great, and the price is significantly less than Dansko. I have a thing about companies that go to China for cheap labor and then continue to ask high prices, or even raise the price (which seems to be happening with Dansko). I've emailed all my nurse friends (MANY!) and recommended that they switch to Sanita: great fit, great value, and it supports European industry. I am naive enough to believe that all of us need to try to stop outsourcing now--keep US and European jobs where they are!

title: Love the Sanita Clog
text: I received my Sanita Clogs today and just love them! They fit well immediately and made my feet feel great, including my foot with a bunion. I had originally purchased a pair of Danskos that looked just like them, as I had owned a pair of Danskos years ago. I did not keep them because they ran too large and I couldn't get the smaller size at the same price. As a result, I ordered the Sanita clogs, not realizing that they were originally a part of Dansko. Sanita still manufactures their shoes in Denmark, whereas Dansko is in China. I'm now sold on Sanita! They ended up being less than the Danskos, too. I will probably order more Sanita shoes in the future.

title: Great shoe but unfortunate sizing
text: I have a pair of Sanitas from years ago, and the 40 fits fine. The 40 in this shoe was simply too tight, with my toes pressed right up against the end. Just received the 41s, and my feet are swimming in them. Am keeping them because I ordered these as house slippers--something I can wear at home without my orthodics. But I wouldn't do any serious walking in them, due to their looseness. I tried on some recent Danskos in a local department store, and they were horrible. The Sanitas are definitely a better shoe.

title: Also (unfortunately) expected from clogs is the sizing issue--I always order the same size and each time I get slightly differen
text: The brown color is darker than I expected, but they are made very well as expected from Sanita. Also (unfortunately) expected from clogs is the sizing issue--I always order the same size and each time I get slightly different variations--sometimes just a tad too large and sometimes perfect (and worst sometimes one side is larger than the other). This time I got slightly larger on both left and right--it's not to the point where I would return them, but I think all clog buyers should know that they tell you since all the clogs are supposedly hand-made there can be intra-size variations in every pair of shoes!

title: First tried on a pair of Danskos at a store then took the plunge and bought Sanita's sight unseen!! PERFECTION!!
text: They fit great on my feet first day out. I have worn them for 11 hours straight with no problem! My foot fits a size 71/2 - 8 shoe (about 9 1/4 inches heel to toe). I have high arches (about a little more than 2 1/4 inches if I am measuring properly), feet are not too narrow not too wide (about 3 3/4 inches at it's widest late at night). I tried on Dansko shoes European size 38 but my feet swam in them (at the end of the day). They felt stiff and very uncomfortable. The woman told me people have to wear them in first, 4 hours one day, then keep them on to watch TV at night, etc et al. It just seemed like a lot of work for a pair of shoes. I bought the Sanita's and wore them right out of the box for a 9 hour hospital shift in the cardiac cath lab. No problems!! My legs felt the same as when I walked in that morning. Actually, after wearing Sanita's all day, it is difficult to wear my Skechers-Bike Hot Ticket sneakers, because the Skechers have no support and are so low to the ground. The color "Rose" is actually a light pink color than what the photo illustrates, which to me looked more like a copper color, which is what I wanted. Totally disappointed in there.

title: Great shoes
text: I wish a would have ordered a size bigger though they were a little tight so I wear thin socks with them, It has really helped my feet when i have been on them all day

title: Love it!
text: I loved my Dansko Pro clogs for the past two+ years and it started to get old looking. After I read comments from other buyers, I decided to get a pair from Dansko and a pair from Sanita for comparison. I have wide and somewhat flat feet, the new Dansko doesn't fit well on my feet (they come off my heels when I walk) but the Sanita fits snuggly like my old Dansko when it was new. This is not something I expected but I am glad that I found my next perfect pair.

title: Sanita clogs are the best!
text: I wear 2 types of shoes...clogs and boots. My Sanitas are, hands down, the best clogs out there! Well constructed, great material, wonderful support and extremely comfortable! (Even helped improve posture, taking pressure off back). Highly recommend!

title: Great for work!
text: The Sanita shoes are made in Europe. Dansko shoes are made in China. That is the reason for choosing this shoe. I wear a 40 or 41. This shoes runs slightly narrow compared to others I have tried. However, it works great with thin socks. I am on my feet all day long. Regardless of your profession ( medical, hairdresser, cashier, groomer) this footbed is a must for those that have to stand all day long. It is approved by the APMA. If you have never worn Sanita or Dansko shoes, the fit is important. They are supposed to be a little loose. You should be able to place your index finger behind your heel. They take a few weeks to mold to your foot. These are a must have if you suffer from aching feet or plantar fasciitis.

title: I love these and the price is great
text: These shoes are not as loose as my Dansko's, but still fit nicely. They are very comfortable. My only slight complaint is that they have a slight squeak, but seems to be improving as I wear them.

title: Love these shoes...
text: Perfect right out of the box! I have been wearing Sanita's for many years and am never disappointed in the quality and fit of these super shoes. I have flat feet and these provide excellent support. I own several pairs of these clogs in various colors and highly recommend Sanita shoes to anyone who has problem feet. It has been my experience that the shoe size fits as expected and this pair is no exception. I was very happy that this pair was on sale. Great shoe, great price.

title: Pretty but not comfortable
text: These were a little snug and you could tell right away they wouldn't be comfortable for wearing all day. My daughter still tried them though since she wanted them to work so much over another pair we picked (these were nicer looking) and wore them for work and her feet and back hurt. She tried the other pair we bought her, Skechers for Work Women's Maisto Elon Oxford, and those ended up being the ones we kept. She was able to work 9 hours on her feet as a cashier without aching feet and back at the end of the day, for once! She loves them and has had them 3 months now. She wished they looked more like these, they're not super fashionable like these are, but in the end she picked comfort and her feet over fashion (who cares at the grocery store how "pretty" your shoes are, right? ha).

title: Great arch support, but heavy
text: These shoe provide great arch support and enough room for toes. But they are very heavy and the heel side is shallow and loose.I feel my legs need to get some effort to keep the feet in the shoes (or maybe it's just slightly too big). I can wear them to work for couple hours and my feet are happy afterward. I got the Asian wide feet, ordered a pair of 7 1/2 (38) W and they fit well.

title: Leather is extremely stiff
text: I was rather bummed out that the leather was so stiff and the shoe felt very uncomfortable. I will be returning them for a credit. I am very disappointed.

title: Skechers Cankton WORK Steel Toe Relaxed Fit Shoes 77055/BKCC - PERFECT & COMFORTABLE
text: I have never had a pair of Steel Toes I didn't hate. I still used them and wore out those I had before I finally bought a Suzuki Boulevard C50T Cruiser motorcycle a couple weeks ago. I wanted a tough sole shoe with a steel toe, especially while I get used to stopping and restarting the bike, but I wanted the shoe to have some feel for the gears and brakes. These Skechers Cankton WORK steel toes were as comfortable as my nicest and most expensive Adidas, New Balance or Reebok tennis shoes, or as any of my street shoes. (I did take out the Skechers insole (only because as a WORK shoe it put more padding under my heel than I needed for riding.) I put in my own favorite brand of insoles for tennis - more arch support, and a little less heel and toe support - and the shoes felt even better. I had a lot more sensitivity to the left foot platform gear shifter, and to the right foot brake on my Cruiser. I would not wear these for tennis, but with these I no longer have to pick my oldest or dirtiest tennis shoes, just to go for a walk in the woods, or in the park after it's rained. I go for rides, I since I don't notice the steel toe at all, I even wear them just to run errands. I normally

title: Although they are a very comfortable steel toe sneaker
text: Although they are a very comfortable steel toe sneaker, they fell apart before they were a year old. the Soles came off the sneaker. My husband only uses these during warm weather and wears a steel toe work boot during the winter, so really he only wore them for approximately six months before they fell apart. I ordered another pair for him and contacted SKECHERS for them to examine the sneakers for being defective. I hope they can resolve this. Amazon did give me a small discount and refunded the shipping fee because of this problem and ordering a new pair.

title: Second pair
text: Purchased these as a backup for a pair I already own. I liked the shoes and wanted a second pair to keep in reserve. I hate having to hunt down and but new shoes - so when I find a pair I like, I try and buy more of them. These shoes are comfortable and seem sturdy enough for the kind of work I do. The size was right for my feet. I'm happy with my purchase.

title: Sole Separates from Shoe in 2 Months.
text: This shoe is adequate at best. If you want a good workshoe that's going to last you a while, look elsewhere. After just 2 months, the sole started to separate from the shoe. Not what I expected when I bought steel toe work shoes that are supposed to be durable. Comfort is okay. Shoelaces are a bit long. Gonna use some JB-Weld to fix the separation issue. Shouldn't have to, though. 2/5.

title: Excellent fit, style, protection, value
text: As usual, Sketchers was true to size and fit comfortably. They look like normal athletic shoes that I wear, and the steel toe provides protection.

title: Great Work Shoe

title: Lasted less than a month. Worn-through insoles, blisters!
text: I like Skechers products, and I have purchased several pairs of their shoes. That said, these steel toe shoes have been an utter disappointment. Like most of Skechers' recent shoes, these feature a memory foam insole. These feel GREAT--for about 3 minutes. Unfortunately, memory foam is heat activated, which means that by the time the shoes warm up, all the foam is softened and provides nearly zero support or cushioning. My feet hurt within 20 minutes of putting them on, and by the end of the day, I'm in agony. Memory foam also means that the shoes have no arch support--zero. The footbed is dead flat. While this may work for people with flat feet, it is unbearable if you have even a moderate arch in your feet, as I do. Again, the memory foam basically melts away when it is warm, so do not expect a comfortable experience. If that wasn't bad enough, the insoles don't last--at all. On day one, the "memory foam" label/decal on the bottom of the insoles began to peel up. They then rolled up and caused irritation and blisters. That wasn't too bad, as I was easily able to peel them off of the insoles once the edge was exposed. The real problem was that my feet wore through the insoles WITH

text: Unfortunately, they do not make this in a 2E, only the 4E. Interestingly, this is not really a true 4E, more like a 3E--as is typical of Nike products, this is narrower than advertised. I need a true 2E from Nike, and a regular D/M width in any other manufacturer (Brooks, Asics, NB). Also, these are a little short for the size. Recommend a half-size up. Note that although this is not indicated anywhere in the product listing, this is a SUPPORT shoe for people who pronate. I supinate slightly (the opposite), so this is not the right shoe for me. Solid shoes though--this is one of the most durable shoes I have ever owned--extremely durable, in fact. You will go through lots of laces before these are worn out. I wore mine for years until I finally got a proper education in supportive footwear. Turns out these are totally the wrong shoe for me and were screwing up my ankles and knees because they increased my supination (rolling of the foot outward), instead of preventing it. I need a "neutral" shoe, and these are a "support" shoe.

title: Why do I keep trying
text: Skechers makes shoes I find visually appealing. They tend to be very comfy right off the bat and they make lots of models in wide sizes. However, their quality is just terrible. I bought these in June for the new school year, but ended up wearing them starting in July because my previous pair of skechers was falling apart. Now only 2 months later, the inside heal of one shoe is wearing out, the loop on the back has already snapped and the memory foam has lost its omph. I guess I but them because the prices are cheap, but not really. They used to be cheap, but when I need to replace them in less than a year, when I used to get 2 years out of them, there's a problem and they become expensive. I'm an adult who mainly used these to walk to work. I don't beat on them. My Mizuno running shoes have a YEAR warranty. title: I have shoes again!
text: My feet can swell big time and I have osteoarthritis in both feet so finding & wearing shoes is hard. For years now I have had to wear Rafters Women's Breeze Skinny Flip Flops as slippers and shoes which are not good for my feet issues and I can no longer find them to purchase. I've looked at shoes for diabetics, but none have fit all my needs and the good quality ones are very expensive. When I saw these I decided to take a chance since they had free returns. The first pair I ordered were my normal, unswollen size: 11 C/D. Because of my swelling they didn't close on the top of my feet. Since I've never had wider than wide shoes I didn't know how they fit so I got the 4E pair instead. Even with really swollen feet they fit nicely and actually made my feet look normal. And as a nice extra benefit, they wider ones were actually much cheaper that day! Very light weight, supportive enough for me, didn't cause me any trouble when walking. The only thing I would change is for them to have BLACK SOLES. I really hate the white (which is why I didn't give them 5 stars) NOTE: if you use the free returns option WATCH YOUR BILLING!! I really like the breathable knit fabric. It keeps my feet cool, and since it has no seams, there is nothing to rub your foot and make blisters. I developed a blister wearing these for long walks which I don't with my women's size ones, but now I just wear them for shorter walks. These are still the same high quality shoe.

Nevertheless, I was expecting I could actually slip them on without a shoehorn and I can't. They are just too stiff and they are oddly thin. They are a medium width, but there isn't enough vertical space for my foot to slide in. Wearing them feels like squeezing my foot in a panini press. I end up with soreness on the top of my foot. I can still wear them from time to time, but I think they are just poorly-made. The design would probably work well with better leather and a nice rubber sole, but it doesn't work right with super stiff leather and a plastic sole because they don't stretch or "break in."

title: These shoes are NOT 2E's
text: Beware, Amazon listed these as 2E on their website but the shoes run narrow and arrive marked W, these shoes are not a true 2E, they are in reality an E width. I know from experience that the catchall W widths almost never fit my wide foot (which is 2E based on accurate store measurement), the reason I chose these shoes is because they were listed as 2E's. Shame on you Amazon for what I consider deceptive marketing, if you are selling a "W" width market it as such, when you market a shoe as a 2E I expect to receive a true 2E. That being said, otherwise the shoes appear fine so if you have an E width foot you will probably be happy with the shoes in a W, I can't speak to the longevity since they don't fit and will be sent back.

I wear size 6.5 and Skechers fit me correctly in my size. They're super easy to slide into; I love that I get a tennis shoe look and feel without having to tie strings. And I love the super cute aqua, yellow, and pink elastics that criss cross the shoe front. They go with lots of my clothes and I wear them often. I broke my right foot last year and it still hurts without good support, and these shoes give me just enough firmness with plenty of cushioning. I own several pairs of Skechers in various styles and I highly recommend them for comfort, support, and value. Their quality is very high; all the pairs I own have held up well to frequent use over the years. They are my go-to brand.

All these years, I needed an 8 1/2 N, not a M. I'm 46 and it's just crazy to me that I never figured this out. I don't dress up very much and the difference between M and N isn't as noticeable in more casual shoes such a flats or sneakers. However, now that I know a N can make such a difference I'm going to search for it when buying shoes. I've rarely seen N in the stores. Grateful to Naturalizer and Amazon for helping me get this great pair of heels that actually fit!

title: Quality of Merrell has slipped, great shoe, poor manufacturing. Get it togther Merrell!!
text: I've bought this shoe for 22 years- love it. I can do a 12 hr shift on my feet with this shoe on. This year the manufacturing has changed. This shoe has always been so reliable for me, get them out of the box and go. Not no more. The hole where the foot goes in is now so small and tight. I sent back 3 pairs and they all had this problem. My foot at the opening felt like it was being strangled. Also the sewing in shoddy. One shoe had a wrinkle sewn into the white foot bed under the sole liner. Just poor quality. I sent them all back and finally went to a local store where I could try them on and totally inspect them before I bought. I found a pair that was just right. I will buy this Jungle Moc probably the rest of my life, but just not online anymore. I don't know what has happened to Merrell's quality, but it has really slipped. I hope they get a hold of the problems soon.

title: What has happened to Merrell?? They used to be so good. Cheap manufacturing !!
text: I recently went back 3 pairs of Merrell shoes. I have been wearing Merrell Jungle Mocs for 22 years, they have always been so reliable and perfectly predictable with fit. Suddenly the manufacturing has changed. I got the first pair and the opening where your foot goes in was so small and tight. Tried another pair, this one was so loose my foot would almost come out of the shoe when I walked. That is NOT my dear Jungle Mocs fit. Next I got another pair and I felt a lump in the heel. I pulled out the sole liner and saw a big ridge sewn into the white foot bed. Poor mfg. Also the right shoe was bigger than the left. Finally I gave up getting them online and went to a shoe store. I now have a new pair of my beloved Jungle Mocs and my feet are ready for a 12 hour shift in health care. I will never order shoes online again. It feels like there's less wear-and-tear on my joints, because the longer range-of-motion my foot goes through reduces the peak force on my body. Great for travel as well. title: Amazing shoe changed my life!
text: This shoe is amazing and I will explain why - When you run, with each step, your body has kinetic energy that must be dispersed when you land on the ground. Energy = Work = Distance * Force When your run with a normal shoe, you land on your heal, which compresses only a few millimeters. The force felt by your body is jarring. If you try to run on the balls of your feet in a normal shoe, your range of motion is limited, perhaps to a couple centimeters. When you run barefoot, or with Vibrams, your range of motion is much larger. Your calf disperses your kinetic energy from the moment the ball of your foot touches the ground to when your heel touches the ground. The force, then, is distributed over 6-to-10 centimeters. The average force on your joints is considerably less with Vibrams than with traditional shoes. Also, the shoes are tiny, light, and great for traveling.

The second issue is breaking in yourself, not necessarily the shoes. Because you now no longer have a higher or cushioned heal on your shoes you will be stretching your calves and other parts of your feet that you didn't know existed. So... TAKE IT SLOW!!! Very slow would be best. I did not remember to heed the warnings and... Boy were my calves and ankles sore the next couple of days. As time progresses you can feel the improvement in your legs and feet.

I only wore them once before the hike so I'm hoping they'll break in a bit more. I had blisters on the bottom of both big toes, but I also wear arch-supporting insoles which may have contributed to the rubbing. They're nice looking boots and one person stopped me on the trail to ask about them. I'm a size 13 and these boots fit fine. I also buy Nikes because I know when I get a size 13, it'll fit as expected. (I've had issues buying other brands, like Adidas, that got a bit smaller than expected.)

title: Finally - Dry Feet
text: Background: I walk the dog every night, rain or shine. Walking a few miles on dirt trails and grass fields. Doesn't sound like much but I manage to destroy shoes in a few months. Since it is winter, the fields have been soaked. I was in desperate need of REAL waterproof shoes. These were the answer. I was impressed by the "Danner-Dry" liner. A logical approach to waterproofing shoes. Yes they work, I was wading through a few inches of standing water without my socks even becoming damp. These boots have a sneaker look and feel. They aren't bulky and heavy. I wear a 11.5 in Vans and a 12 in Nike's. I ordered both an 11 and 11.5 because of other reviews saying they ran slightly large, these reviews were accurate. The 11 fit like a glove, but only with standard crew socks. They were very comfortable. I did want to have the option to wear a thicker sock with these when I am in the snow, so I went for the 11.5. Couldn't be happier. They are comfortable no mater what socks I am wearing, plenty of room without feeling loose. The quality of the materials and build are top notch. Bit pricey, but you can't really put a dollar amount on dry feet! I will be purchasing Danner boots from now on.

title: Very comfortable, sturdy
text: Been wearing these about a year, ?150 miles or so, maybe a lot more. Use - 40:60 pavement vs. wooded trails. Very comfortable, sturdy, not heavy. I wish that the soles would have lasted longer but I suspect that this is about as good as it gets these days. At least there's been no separation between the sole and boot and the stitches are all holding. Addendum: August 30, 2018. Changed the insoles to Spenco Rx thin lightweight. A thicker insole (Insole for Men's dress shoes (Amazon choice) were too thick. I do have a narrow foot and again these boots are quite good. I'm upgrading them from 4 stars to 5. Addendum November 5, 2018. Soles have separated and were wearing through in the heel. I bought a new pair. Will followup in time again. Good value. Nothing lasts forever, not these days anyhow. Addendum January 21, 2019. 2nd pair is better than I remember the first pair being. Warm, feet stay dry, great grip from soles on uneven surfaces. Insoles are fine while new. Not heavy.
