title: Really nice shoes!
text: Finally found a Merrell shoe I like! Their designs and colors have always been a put off to me. But this pair in the dark gray, I really like a lot. I wear these all the time and they have good arch support and comfortable to walk around in. Plus they are waterproof and perfect to wear during winter in Chicago. I also bought a different color boot by Merrell which I don’t find as comfortable as this shoe! But that’s another review. Also Amazons price for these was great compared to buying in a store. So that made it even better.

title: Awesome shoe
text: I’ve been a Merrell fan for years and the shoe is super for all my outdoor activities. Add to that the price I got them for- i scored!

title: Junk
text: Merrill’s definitely have gone downhill quality wise. They used to last forever and be super comfortable. Now they hurt your feet and start falling apart in months. So sad how so many companies cheap out like this once they have a name, all just to please stockholders.

title: Good fit, a little clunky, terrible support
text: Not my first Merrell's. I also wear Salomon, North Face, and Keen hikers and these Merrell's ahve the best fit for a wide foot, in terms of width. They also have the WORST support -- or complete lack thereof. First wearing these shoes for about a 2 mile walk on a developed trail (to break them in, which they DO require), my feet felt like they'd been hammered with steel after less than an hour. Terrible, terrible heel and arch comfort/support. I put some Oboz insoles in and that helps tremendously. However, it also lifts my heel so that the shoes don't fit properly. I have the same problem in terms of fit after adding insoles with my Salomon Ultras, so not totally unexpected. Keen Targhee (two different generations) still fit well after adding after-market insoles. Keen also has a great wide fit, but their shoes are known to fall apart due to low quality glue. So... Merrell might still be the better choice, due to the Vibram sole, which I can attest to lasting a long time. We'll see whether these Merrell's remain waterproof -- the Keens are the most waterproof boots I've even found and the Salomon's are great, too (though too narrow for a truly wide foot? and thin material makes fo

title: 1/2 size large fits me.
text: Shoes fit beautifully... normally wear size 11. Took a chance on 11 1/2. Very comfortable.

title: Buy them a little big
text: SO here's the deal. I had two pairs of these- as I really like them. One said size 12 and the other said 10-1/2. Both fit about the same! I have never worn a 10-1/2 before these, usually 11-1/2, but I find Asian made products to have wacky sizes. Best to try them on. Anyway, like a bonehead, I bought 10-1/2 and UNLIKE my past pair, they are tight. Took a few days for me to decide that. I thought they might stretch....but no, they don't. Totally MY BAD, I should have returned them, but I didn't. Wish I had..., they are not cheap (for me, anyway). I only wear them for short hikes, because they are not so comfortable. ---> Moral of the story--Buy them a little big, NEVER small.

title: Love the shoe, but it runs small.
text: Love the shoe, but it runs small. My husband normally wears 12D which is what we ordered. Tight width wise and his toe was hitting the end length wise so we ordered a 13E. Hopefully the larger one will fit.

title: Great shoe. Durability-TBD
text: So the fit was great. The support that I was looking for in a daily shoe is excellent. I've had Merrells in the past and I used them for work shoes. The comfort and durability were outstanding. I'm hoping that these Moab 2's can repeat that kind of performance. I like that they're waterproof and so far, they seem very well built and comfortable. I will edit as time passes to update on durability. Later edit: A difficult rock climb up Blue Mountain, and these shoes passed with flying colors. Still waterproof, very steady on uneven surfaces, rocks, roots and extreme ascent and descent. No hotspots, no blisters, very comfortable. I'm liking them a lot. Later later edit: I've now had them for a year and a half. I wear them to work every day. I've flattened out the treads through wear, put them through the mill, wet use, hard use, hiking too... and they've come through. No separations. Waterproofing is still basically intact. I've smooshed out the insoles pretty well and probably need to put an insert in but they're still very comfortable and though looking a bit the worse for wear cosmetically they are still going strong and very intact. I feel that though these were on the expensive s

title: Poor quality stitching. Broke on first use.
text: I liked the look and fit of these shoes when I got them. I tried them on around the house for a day and only had a small amount of discomfort from the left shoe's tongue rubbing my foot, but I was able to fix this by repositioning the tongue and forcing the fabric flaps in a different direction. The issue came when I went to lace them up to actually use them. As I was tightening the left shoe the tongue lace eyelet came unstitched. It didn't tear or break: it just came out of the stitching. See photo. Unfortunately I had to send these back and there wasn't another pair available in this color in my size. I'll be looking around for something else. From other reviews I've seen that the quality of these newer versions aren't as good as the old versions. I can attest to this.

title: Merrell makes a good shoe!
text: I've bought a lot of Merrell's over the years. And I"m not sure if my foot is getting bigger (like the rest of me!) or these are getting smaller. But this is the first pair I've gotten that I felt were too snug. They might stretch out but so far they're a bit tight. Quality-wise, they're what you expect from Merrell: good quality, well-made, no loose strings, etc. I've bought this exact pair before and was very pleased with the life of them. Used them for everything from everyday use around town to moderate hiking.

title: Good fit but 2 heavy 4 me
text: Still looking for Merrell to replace my All Out Blaze original. Moab2 wide fits well but is just too heavy for me. Had to return. Hope Merrell comes out with another shoe like the original All Out Blaze with wide toe, sewed insole and light weight. All Out Blaze 2 does not work for me.

title: Toe Box Way Too Tight
text: I double dog dare you to break these shoes in before the pain is so bad in the underside of your foot next to your little toes that you scream while you are taking them off and finally throwing these in the trash can because you, even after repeated attempts at wearing them and trying to break them in so you could comfortably wear them for more than six hours have failed miserably. Buy Keen boots and you won’t waste you money on Merrell shoes again.

title: Very comfortable hiking shoes
text: Sturdy and comfortable. A good quality shoe. I really don't like ordering shoes online because I am afraid they won't fit right but I needed the hikers right away and my town doesn't offer anything worth buying. I was pleased that they fit perfectly.

title: The most comfortable hiking boot I've ever owned
text: Hands down, the best hiking boot I've worn. No break-in time at all, and they were first tested running on a treadmill, then an 8-mile hike up a mountain the first time I wore them outside; no blisters. Also, I'm prone to a lot of toe pain when I hike, to the point where I have bruised toes and my toe nail eventually falls off, but absolutely no bruising of my toes and very minimal toe pain was incurred on that 8-mile hike I mentioned earlier. I loved these so much, I bought my partner the male version and he was just as blown away by them.

title: Five Stars
text: I found these boots very comfortable and are great for walking the dog especially on those wet days.

title: runs a bit small but very comfortable shoe
text: Toe box wider than some other shoes, which is good. Good hiking shoe at good price

title: left shoe has uncomfortable lump towards heel. Hope this is an isolated problem.
text: Left shoe has uncomfortable lump towards heel. Hope this is an isolated problem.

title: My favorite boot. 2nd pair in 12 years
text: I like every about these boots. Needed no breaking in. Fun color, waterproof tested already!!

title: Highly recommend!
text: Perfectly comfortable right out of the box. I had tried several pairs before I found these and had no time to "break then in". I got theses the day I had to be on the range on my feet all day for 3 days in a row.

title: Love Merrill's but Arch in wrong position
text: This is my third pair of Merriell products. I have ankle boots, Cafe/knee boots and now these hiking boots. In the past I thought the arch support was in a slightly in a weird position. I thought it was just me but other reviews have mentioned the same thing. I generally have to remove the insoles and put my own molded orthoficts in the boots. Have to buy high quality over the counter ones to do I don't have to keep changing them out of my shoes and boots. Merrels insoles are pretty nice though. I have worn a pair of boots with the original insoles before and survived. Interesting that I have not had this problem with the arch placement in any other line of shoes before. Still I love Merrell shoes for the wider toe box. Wearing these hiking shoes at Iguazu Falls since it is very slippery there. Breaking them in hiking in the woods at home and a short trip to Quebec first. I'm happy that with these boots I can wear thick wool hiking socks and my molded orthodicts comfortably by sizing up to a wide and a half size larger. For your information I am generally between a 10 medium or a 10 wide. I got a 10 1/2 wide. Off topic: I did not have the option of half sizes with my other "dressie

title: Cold and Wet Weather' Friend
text: Hood for cold and wet weather, might be too hot in warmer weather due to the waterproofing. I've worn out and about in 50-60+ weather and my feet got hot.

title: So Comfortable!!
text: I have very sensitive feet when it comes to shoes. My feet are very flat and slightly wide and these were perfect! I purchased these in 6.5 (true to size) in both wide and regular and found the regular fit fantastically with my wool socks. I wore these for a week in Iceland and they were truly waterproof in streams and they kept my feet comfortably warm. I would highly recommend these!

title: true to size good quality
text: I ordered 1/2 size big so I could wear thicker socks. It's very comfortable. highly recommend.

title: Finally
text: I have flat feet with a bunion on one. Need a large toe box. I ordered up one half size as recommended. Then bought arch supports online. Had to buy a second larger set of supports for one shoe as the medium one didn't quite hit my arch in the right location. After all was said and done they are perfect!!! Actually returned my super fancy LL Bean Gortex hikers. These merells have solved my hiking boot dilemma. They work really well on the rocky Maine trails where I live.

title: Stylish and rugged
text: Lightweight and comfortable for hiking for my partner. She is really pleased with these as they are wider then some and just right.

title: My favorite part of hiking...
text: is putting on these boots. I absolutely love them and am so glad I purchased them. I took them with me to a Canadian winter, and they were waterproof and WARM and so incredibly comfortable. Right out of the box, they were soft yet supportive, rigid and cushy in all the right places. Couldn't be more pleased.

title: Fit Seems Really Off
text: Used Merrel hikers for years...this model was not at all like previous quality. Uncomfortable & right boot seemed irregular in the seams.

title: Comfortable Boot, No Traction In Damp Conditions
text: This is my second pair of these boots. They’re incredibly comfortable, don’t hurt after a day of hiking, and give great arch support. When we lived in Florida and Texas, these did everything I needed. But now in Japan, these boots are not cutting it. Wet or damp rocks cause the boots to lose all traction. A little bid of mud? No traction. Even wet concrete, no traction. I thought the boots were old and I just needed a new pair, but I’m still running into the same problem. I’ve slipped and fallen due to the boots more than I care to admit. This last fall was pretty nasty and I’m thankful I haven’t broken anything. What’s worse is there seem to be plenty of others on the trails in just sneakers who have no problem. My point is, if you’re hiking somewhere with wet or damp terrain, you might not like these boots either. Otherwise, they’re fantastic.

title: Wide width is perfect
text: I am a small woman with wide feet. For decades I have searched for a pair of hiking boots that fit properly...I finally found them. Most brands don't offer a wide and if they do they are too wide for me. These boots are just right. My toes can spread out but they are not so wide my feet slip around. The lacing system keeps laces secure. The rugged soles are great for rough terrain. I have very high arches and wish they had more arch support but for the average foot I'm sure they would be fine. I also wish they were a little lighter, as a small person they feel slightly heavy. I took them on a week long hiking vacation and had no blisters or pain points...no breaking-in time needed.

title: 8 + hours of Comfort, offers Support, and Breathable when walking on loose terrain.
text: Very comfortable and a nice roomy toe box. I walk on large loose gravel at work, very supportive. This is my first pair of Merril shoes, and it won't be my last. I ordered the 9.5 and is very true to size.

title: LOVE these boots
text: LOVE these boots. Super comfy with a fairly wide toe box. First time wearing them I went on a 7 mile hike and they were perfect.

title: Get em! Worth it
text: These are amazing. They were comfy straight out of the box. Ive been wearing them all winter too because the traction is so good. I have a wide foot and feet issues. These are great. 100% buy.

title: Very nice hiking boot!
text: I have ordered 3 different hiking boots and this one was Perfect! All others went back.

title: Merrell is a good experience!
text: Bought these boots to replace a 15 year old pair that split. They were also Merrell and I hated throwing them away however they had served well! These boots are a great replacement, I love them. No break in period, I wore them on my daily 2 - 3 mile walk and they were very comfortable right away! Merrell rarely lets me down! They are very warm and fit perfectly! I always wear a size 7 and although some reviews suggested going up 1/2 size I did not and I am very glad I didn't. I do wear slightly thick smart wool socks and they still fit very nicely. Although these are waterproof and warm I do not think they will do ice well but that is ok, I have since bought another pair more specifically for snow and ice. Also Merrell.

title: Im a fan
text: Found a pair of hiking shoes that is great straight out of the box. Weighs between 1.5-1.8 lbs. Looks a tad bulky but it’s lightweight with good ankles support. The insoles are a little thinner on the forefeet for me so i switched it with my Salomon’s and it feels Better. Motherload of all boots indeed!

title: Love my new Hiking boots
text: Great fit right out of the box. I did go up 1/2 size because I didn't want "to break them in" but there is no need to. I truly love the fit especially how they fit my "weak" ankles.

title: Love these boots
text: They fit perfectly right out of the box. If you're going to hike in the summer months they are a bit hot but that was to be expected. I ordered a 7.5 and I usually wear a 7.5 and they fit perfect. I do have narrow feet and ankles just for reference.

title: Good fit and strong and supportive boot
text: Always a gamble to order shoes online. I wear a 10 with a little wide foot. So ordered 10W. Fit's perfectly. Excellent support. I will take these hiking through Central America, and feel confident that they will be comfy and supportive. I would expect excellent quality for the price. Worth it to pay for quality.

title: Kinda crappy but better than nothing
text: It's hard to find well-made, good fitting shoes these days. While these are better than nothing, they still don't fit or walk as well as Merrells used to before they moved production to China. sigh. The inserts flatten very fast (had to replace them almost immediately) and the overall construction of the shoe is just a little on the ill-fitting side and not built for any measure of comfort. Too bad--Merrell used to be awesome and now, 3 stars is generous.

title: Perfect!
text: I have been ordering boots to hike in and sending them back for the past two weeks. Finally these arrived and they are perfect! They even have great arch support, and I have very high arches. There is a big arch support on the inside of each boot - if you don't have high arches, these might be uncomfortable. I love the vibram soles - I've been hiking two hours a day since the beginning of May in the woods and it can be slippery especially going downhill, and these soles are wonderful. Also before these boots I was twisting my ankles almost every day. These have super support for my ankles, and I am really glad I got them! Also the olive color with the purple laces just makes me happy.

title: Lightweight and comfortable!
text: This pair came surprisingly comfortable and soft! I am size 6-6.5 and I ordered 6.5, which gives me more room for wearing thick socks. The arch support is very good, toe box is roomy, so when going down the mountain your toes won’t feel squeezed. My daughter used to always complain about feet hurting and say her legs dead after hiking in her regular sneakers as she didn’t want to wear heavy hiking boots. Till I bought this pair and asked her to wear them for a hike to Mt. Minsi, she listened and didn’t have the complaint about feet hurting after. And yesterday we hiked to the Pulpit Rock and the Pinnacle, she was wearing this pair, she didn’t complain at all! I am going to buy another pair for myself right after writing this review. Happy hiking to all!

title: Make sure you don't need a wide. These boots run narrow.
text: It's been awhile since I bought shoes and apparently my feet are now wide. In truth, they're really not all that wide. A guy at Big 5 says all shoes are running smaller than they used to. If you were to look at my feet and guess, you wouldn't call them "wide." But Merrell knows best. I guess my feet are wide in Merrell World. They might wide be in your world, too. I bought two pairs of these boots, a 9 and a 9.5. I'm going to have to send both back due to how very narrow they are.

title: Lack of Mid-Sole Support?
text: I purchased these after buying TWO pairs of 'Fila's that were on sale on JC Penny's and found them 'functional but could be better" . The reason for buying shoes from this user is for walking- and by that I mean walking about 7 miles every morning and often 3-5 miles later in the day as well. The pair I have liked is a DOUBLE FUSION by Nike that provides soft but firm support for the entire foot from HEAL to TOE and Mid-Sole. The Fila's just feel 'flat' and do not provide the support or cushion this user needs since I have no cartilage left in my knees and hips. Therefore, cushioning and support both are of prime importance (I'm a former long distance runner who averaged over 100 miles/week at one point). The Saucony I read averages 'small' so best to order 1/2 size larger than one's usual (that is what I read in comments)...so that is what I did. Must say, size wise (width/length) of this shoe in doing so, couldn't be much better. My only complaint on this end is the mid-sole feels a bit 'flat or hard' as I'd hope it would be. I did purchase at the Dollar Store (of all places) this extra thick insole to line along the bottom of the shoe and that made a big difference.

title: Four Stars
text: I’ve always enjoyed both Saucony and New Balance brands style and fit. Saucony has the edge on price.

title: I wear a FULL SIZE larger in Saucony
text: Great shoe. Most of my shoes, I wear a 10-1/2 men's size. I always get size 11-1/2 when ordering Saucony running shoes. I don't run anymore, but wear these all day for comfort.

title: Too small
text: I would like to return them and purchase another pair that fit. I need an wide 10.5. What do I do first?

title: Inaccurate sizing
text: Wear 9M so I ordered 10M because these types of shoe run small, guess what one shoe measures and 8 1/2 Narrow and the other is a 9 narrow, I ordered a 10M?????

title: replaced my favorite old Saucony's and didn't let me down.
text: This is my second pair of Saucony's. The first pair where my favorite running shoe of all time. I would always kid and say it was like walking on marshmallows because of the plush feel. This pair does feel a little more sturdy and definitely has more support than the previous pair. For the price I would imagine it would be hard to find a better quality running shoe. I would definitely recommend find these if you want an inexpensive pair with good support.

title: excellent shoe
text: I have one foot about one size larger than the other, a narrow heel, and am pigeon toed. This model of Saucony and a similar Asics are able to be excellent on the 12 foot and good on the 11+ foot. avoid heel slip and slightly correct my pigeontoedness. The Asics are just a little too gaudy for me and have mostly white sides on the soles that I do not like. Both have just a little excess space in the toe box, but not uncomfortably so for walking, but might be for running. Both have what I call two extra eyelets at the top and I use the top one to pull and lace very tight and help with heel slip.

title: Great running shoe. I don't run but I like Saucony's...
text: I have purchased several Saucony's over the years. Great shoes. This pair just isn't wide enough for me. I'll live with it and try to order different the next time if I can.

title: Comfort and stability in a lightweight shoe.
text: These are for me, the most comfortable shoes that I wear. I have about eight pair of them.. And nothing is better than a new pair!

title: Comfortable
text: I love this brand, these are very comfortable and support my feet well. I use them for running on asphalt. The shoe tends to rub my left ankle for some reason though.

title: Five Stars
text: Good durable shoes for my son. They fit well and are holding up after several months of wear.

title: Nope!
text: I love giving great reviews but honestly, this is my second pair of the Cohesion Model Saucony's and they just aren't comfortable. First Pair I bought is at least seven years old and I still wear them on occasion. I ordered the same size this time and they pinch my feet as if they aren't really Wide's? I will just give them to my son. His feet are narrow and he will likely love them.

title: Love these
text: I've had three pairs of these because they look good, are inexpensive, and feel great. Not many shoes fit my feet. I put an insole to get a bit better cushion and arch support.

title: Ok for the price
text: Product is ok. Not comparable to past saucany shoes I have had in the past (costing double to triple the price $100-$120). The best comparison I can make is if you go to the outlet for a designer product for a discounted price. Looks like the product, but quality isint there. Ok for the gym and running moderately. Would not recommend if you run everyday.

title: 50k worthy
text: Ran two 50k’s and many training runs in these cheap things, they’re great and the toe box is wide enough to avoid tearing your feet up. Anyone who says they fall apart must be running strangely

title: no running needed
text: The shoes fit is good, light and flexible no break in needed,, I got the blue and they look good.

title: Put them on and get moving! Very comfortable.
text: Ordered and received on time. Super comfortable. Normally break in by walking a mile or less for the first few days. Not this time, put two miles on first walk and no soreness after. Next day three. Great shoes.

title: Could not be happier with my Saucony shoes!!!
text: Have worn them a few times, but am very pleased with them so far. Fit is just fine. They give my feet plenty of support and my feet do not seem to get tired as rapidly as they do with other shoes I wear. Most of my other shoes make my feet feel "tired" and needing relief by taking them off after more then 6/7 hours of wear. My Saucony Cohesion 10 Running shoes still are comfortable after 8 yours of use. Wish Saucony made a shoe suitable for dress wear. I would snap up them up in a heartbeat.

title: Whole the accommodate a wide foot there is not enough ...
text: Whole the accommodate a wide foot there is not enough sole horizontally to support the outside of my feet causing rolling. No go for me

title: Great shoes for the price
text: I have owned Sauconys in the past and found them to hold up better than some other brands. These are soft and comfortable with good cushioned insoles. Wil definitely buy another pair.

title: Great running shoes
text: These shoes fit very well and are very comfortable. I bought the wide version. I am using my own orthotics insert. Shoe inserts supplied by the manufacturer are never good.

title: Great Shoe
text: I really like these shoes. They are just perfect. And the price was especially nice. Highly recommended.

title: Vibrant blue color
text: The size was as expected and this is a comfortable shoe. The blue color is a bit more vibrant than the picture depicts. Would have preferred if it were darker or a bit more subdued.

title: Good support
text: I have a very wide foot and these are comfortable and provide good walking support.

title: Tight
text: I normally wear a 11.5 EE in both New Balance and Merrell, but these were WAY snug when I put them on. Uncomfortably tight really. Snug in length also- easily a 1/2 size size smaller for me. However- Nice shoes and delivered right on time so I can't complain ( free return).

title: Nice comfortable shoes.
text: These were extremely comfortable for my son. He has medium width feet with a pretty normal arch. He is 12 and finding comfortable enough shoes is usually a chore. He loves these and they look really nice.

title: Not a running shoe, but good nonetheless.
text: I wouldn't plan on running any long distances in these; these are really more of a work/referee/coaching shoe. They fit well, and are reasonably comfortable, it appears to be well made. Extremely lightweight. I certainly would not use them for running though. I wear them on a daily basis to work, and for the price, I bought two pair and I switch them out about every six months. For $40, you really can't beat that. The all-black look goes well with the government uniform I have to wear.

title: Quality not what I hoped for
text: With the very many excellent reviews, I really had high hopes that I would have found a sneaker my feet might delight to call home. I was truly looking forward to putting them on. Then I did. What a disappointment. First, the quality was not even close to what I had been led to expect. They were very sparse in comfort, and the shell of the upper around the front of the foot was almost like a simple hard, plastic lining. Nothing inviting about it at all. To make it worse, my feet are, like many, of slightly different sizes, with my left being the larger of the two. In this case, the first shoe I tried was the left, and that went well. Much was my surprise, then, when I put on the right and found my toes pressing against the outside of the toe-box. It only got worse when I stood up and walked in them. It was painful, and what I am led to believe is that the shoe was simply not the right size, though it was labeled as such. In all, I have found other shoes to be much more comfortable, even if they in the end were not shoes I ultimately purchased. This pair, as some other reviewers have pointed out, was not anywhere near the quality that was expressed in the reviews. Did the manufactur

title: Great value
text: Shoes are great. They fit as expected and we're bargain priced. Ordered them amidst a cross-country trip for my son when his old shoes fell apart. Very happy with the choice.

title: Beware, I was charged for Return Shipping.
text: I Googled a running shoe for knee pain and this was one of the top least expensive shoes. After two meniscus surgeries I have knee pain after running. I was surprised w how lightweight and supportive this shoe is. It's a neutral shoe but it provides great arch support( I have a medium arch). I've been using it primarily as a treadmill shoe, I use a Asics Nimbus & Brooks GTS w more cushioning for my outdoor runs. But lately it has been doing double duty as an around the house shoe because its lightweight & comfortable. I wear an 11.5 and the fit was good, w a thumb space at the toe. I took away 2 stars because this shoe states it's Free Return but when I tried to return a larger size( purchased 2 diff. sizes), the seller charged me over $5.00 for the return shipping. When I mentioned the free return I was told that, "The return shipping cost is listed in the details (meaning, "the fine print"). I thought this was very misleading. Please beware.

title: Saucony shoes are the best for the person I buy them for
text: These are for Christmas gift so they haven't been tried on yet. But if they are the same as I have ordered before they will be great.

title: WHY TWO stars when I LOVE Saucony brand
text: I have multiple pairs of Saucony. I wear them for working out, walking, running errands. Unless I am getting dressed up, my shoe of choice (and have been since 1990's when I realized they were a better fit, out of the box, than any of the other leading brands). My Experience: FIT - still fit out of the box. I wear an 8.5 in Saucony's and no matter which style I get, they fit. HOWEVER, the left insole is considerably higher than right. Just not comfortable and you're constantly aware of it. COMFORT - OK comparing these to the Cohesion 11 (which I have two pairs of), not nearly as much comfort, cushion. And like I mentioned, left insole higher, so just weird and wonky walking or running in these. QUALITY - overall, quality seems higher on the Cohesion 11, just looking at upper shoe, and how much more cushion the 11 has. So lower quality than the 11 overall. COLOR - The purple color is WHY I ordered these over the Cohesion 11. I figured the 10 would be similar and the 10 had the GREAT purple color, the 11 didn't. But it isn't the color that is what you're walking on! PRICE - EVEN though less cushion than the Cohesion 11, I would have kept them if the insole in left wasn't so different

title: Speed inhancer
text: These improved my speed. I can run super fast now. Before I was just fast now I'm super fast.

title: Happy Feet

Kudos to New Balance for coming out with the new version of 410s 5 years, or so, later. They're perfect in every way. I've purchased 4 pairs in the last month. Stocking up.

In fact there was only 1 problem. The sole was not any sort of grip material. Most soles of closed toe shoes are some sort of rubber or ect that makes you feel safe and that you won’t slip when you walk on non carpeted surfaces. I slipped on my laminate flooring. I was so bummed that I decided to walk around a bit- see if I might even be able to scrape it off. The important parts of the sole were like fuzzy. I think where your arch would be was normal rubber- but that didn’t help me from not slipping. My laminate flooring isn’t even as slippery as say Target flooring or grocery store floor so I knew I had to return them. I hope they fix this issue and put out the style again because everything else was great.

title: A note for narrow feet
text: My rating is particular to the fit for ME, not a commentary on the quality - this shoe is amazingly constructed, looks classy on, and for leather, you can't beat the price. Stitching and gluework was excellent. While I agree that sizing up half a size would be great for those with broader feet, I also agree that you should get your normal size because even wearing these for 15 minutes, I saw that they were malleable and probably fit better with time. My specific issue is that with narrow feet, the toebed is wonderful, but if you ALSO have no arch, you have to tie the laces at the absolute tightest they go - so for me, it would be too large in the ankle opening and where the leather comes together in tying. Too bad for me, because these would be perfect otherwise! But if you've a low clearance in terms of the 'height' of your foot, these probably won't work for you. It's not the sole width that is the issue, but the shoe height.

title: Beware of sizing
text: Although these shoes look great for the price, the sizing is really odd. I normally wear a size 8 (US) in shoes, but the pair I got was more like a 7--I could just barely get my foot into the shoe. So I sized up to a 9. Although my foot now fits in the shoe, the toe area could still use a bit more room. I'd say their 9 is more like a 7.5. Also, the 2nd pair I got appears like someone else tried it on before me--the shoes were out of their protective sleeves and there's minor creasing near the heel as if worn. The heels were clean. I've seen a few reviews state that this shoe is in a solid color, but I can confirm that the 2 pairs I received were both dark brown ombre at the toe.

title: These look amazing with pants

I was looking for a two tone that I could wear with my work pants, but still be eye catching. These look amazing with pants, leggings, skirts/dresses, and even shorts. Basically, I have found many ways to utilize them in my wardrobe. They heel is higher, but it actually adds some arch support to the design. There is no odd smell to them, or crumbling rubber sole. The laces are stiff and needed a lot of fussing, but not enough to remove a star. If the brand can last a few months on my feet, I will buy another color!

title: Far prefer this model to the Kayano 25
text: I have worn Gel Kayanos for years and I feel that I speak from pretty good experience. I far prefer this model of Kayano to the newer Kayano 25 which was redesigned. There are two reasons for this: 1) The Kayano 23 (this one) has more gel padding in the midfoot than the Kayano 25. This shoe, has two visible gel pads on the outer midfoot, whereas for the Kayano 25 the midfoot gel is all inside. I tend to strike on my heel, and then roll on the outer midfoot and back inward to the toe. So I need heel, midfoot, and toe cushioning. The 23 feels way more comfortable than the 25. 2) The Kayano 23 has a narrower toe box than the Kayano 25. While some people may like a wider toe box, I do not because I find my feet are moving around too much in the Kayano 25 which leads to less stability in my run. My foot, which is normal width, fits snugly in the Kayano 23 and doesn't slide around which I prefer. I will continue to purchase "old" model Kayanos as long as they are available. I don't think the new Kayano 25 is better; I think it's less plushy, and a worse fit.

So much so it is uncomfortable and I have to kick them off sometimes due to pain. Have been wearing several weeks now and they have not stretched out a bit to relieve that issue.

title: Very comfortable and easy to put on. Great for doing yard work too.
text: Fits really well and is very comfortable to wear. Had this years before as a "hand me down" and loved it ever since.

title: On my second pair. I will never go to laces again.
text: First off, this is the second pair I have order. The first pair lasted quite a long time and I only abandoned them due to a greasy mishap on my part. I liked the first pair so much I ordered a second pair. When I got the second pair I was a little worried due to a little heel rubbing on one foot. Once they were broken in no problems. The waterproofness(is that a word?) has not let me down. Breathability wise I have never had any waterproof shoes that breath well. You have to expect some give and take. The rubber sole is plenty durable and lasts a substantial amount of time. No complaints there. They tend to run true to size. You definitely don't want to buy the wrong size. My only complaint is side support. They start out great but tend to lose side stiffness and can roll on you.

title: Collapsed back of heel.
text: Initially they seemed like a good choice because they are comfortable. Two disadvantages are that they are warm, and this pair will be returned because one shoe developed a a fault after only three wearings. The back of one shoe collapsed even though I use a shoehorn.

title: Great quality and durable!!!
text: Although we had to reorder a half size smaller, my husband loves these shoes!!! They are great for working around the house and going out casually. Would buy again!!

title: Fit as expected, but didn’t hold up as well as I had hoped
text: I am a 300 pound guy, so I’ve learned not to expect longevity in my shoes. I’ve had this brand and style before, and they served me very well. (Basically that means one year of use) This pair began coming apart barely 3 months into use at the toe where the rubber wraps over the top and is glued. Disappointed in the performance of this pair, but I will buy this brand and style again. I’ll probably simply opt for the non-waterproof version, at about half the cost.

title: Great Tread, Small Opening
text: With a small opening for your foot, these are tough to just slip on; I need a shoe horn. Great tread pattern for most walking and hiking. Nice color but the suede scuffs easily.

title: Surprisingly low quality
text: Really disappointed. They survived about a month and a half. Had to replace the sole after a couple of weeks. I'm glad I didn't buy them for the higher price on the website. DO Not Buy These. By far the worst ones I've owned. So far Carhart seems to have the best.

title: With the Merrell name, these should should be better made.
text: This is my FOURTH pair of Merrell Mocs. The three previous pairs were all Merrell Jungle Mocs. This is my first pair of the Adventure Mocs. That being said, I must admit, I'm somewhat disappointed with the quality of the new Adventure. Granted, it has a nice leather upper finish but the structural support is lacking for shoes that are touted to be "slip ons." The very first time I attempted to slide my feet into these shoes, the back of the shoes collapsed. I was rather surprised and annoyed. I removed the shoes and firmed up the back of the shoes again before attempting to put my feet in again. This time, I used my thumb as a "shoe horn" to slide my feet in. No, I did not have these types of issues with the Jungle Mocs. In fact, the back of the shoes seemed to be more reinforced than the Adventure model. I will continue to wear them but will be more careful with the back of the shoes. PROS: Nice leather uppers, incredibly comfortable CONS: Structural support is lacking

title: Runs small and narrow.
text: I have had Merrill before of this size, and they are perfect. The “ tongue” on these comes up too high and punches the foot. There is no way you could wear them with socks, let alone change to a plantar fasciitis arch support.

title: Great fit for guys with wide feet.
text: I’ve only worn them once at this point, but they fit great and seem to be well made. I have a wide foot with a very high instep, so I’m always concerned that shoes will be to narrow or cut into the top of my foot, but these feel good.

title: Man I Love These Shoes
text: This is my second pair. I wear a size 12. I've had my first pair for three or four years and they're still going strong. The soles have hardly worn down at all. Honestly, the soles of these shoes are probably the best of any shoes I've ever owned. Far, far more durable than rubber soles. They look great, fit great, very comfortable, and the leather is very durable. Thanks Merrell. So long as the quality remains strong, I will keep buying your shoes.

title: Much better sole but different fit than Jungle Moc
text: Summary: Comfortable alternative to the Jungle Moc with a better sole, but fit isn't quite the same. I've had about 4 pairs of Merrell Jungle Mocs over the years, and I still love them, but the soles have poor tread and wear out quickly - an issue when walking or gardening with mud, etc. The Vibram sole on these is much more aggressive and should wear far better than the soft rubber on the Jungle Mocs. I normally wear a size 9 Jungle Moc, and in the Adventure Moc I wear a size 8.5 wide - the size 9 felt narrow and the 9W was too big. For now it appears there isn't a waterproof version of the Adventure Moc, but The Nubuck leather should also take waterproofing better than Suede.

title: About a week, and very comfortable
text: Been wearing for about a week, but most of the time I sit at a desk. So far these are very comfortable. A little loose in the heel area for me, but not enough to be uncomfortable. Nice simple design, which I prefer. Hoping they will last. This is my 3rd pair of Merrill's, and I have not had any issues with any of them.

title: Didn’t work out!

title: These are great shoes

title: Fits a bit large

The color and design makes it more versatile for smart casual use cases but I am not sold on the front design on the sole which appears more fragile and less water proof. It's a great pair of shoes but I think I will try getting Winter Mocs again for my next pair.

title: Quality is good and the Merrel lasts are size consistent
text: These mocs hold up really well. I live rurally and these are my "slippers" that I wear all the time when home. The quality is solid, they breathe reasonably well and they are comfortable. The sole holds up well and has good traction. I'm a heavy guy and soles tend to wear quickly but these are solid material and not slippery. I'm a size 15 and large shoe lasts are outrageously inconsistent where some shoes I wear a 13 and others a 14 or 15 and even within the same manufacturer's line, there are inconsistencies. With Merrel, across their line, their lasts are consistent, so I can just mail order pairs and they just fit fine when I get them.

title: Not a great slide.
text: These were not a great slide for me based on fit and comfort. These slides are definitely on the small side and I recommend ordering one size up. There is also an issue with the holes in the soles if you wear these anywhere except a locker room, which I'm sure most people who order these will do. I understand the purpose of the holes is to drain water since these are a locker room slide, but wearing these outside has the opposite effect because particles end up coming into the holes and lodging in the foot bed. It is uncomfortable to wear these outside the house. These also wore down quickly and ended up in the trash within a month. I don't recommend these for anything besides a true locker room sandal and nothing more. Update: I ordered a second pair of these, against my better judgment, because I needed a pair of water shoes for a vacation. I stand by my original review. These fit on the small side and the holes in the foot bed allow particles to come up.

title: Highly Satisfied Customer
text: This was for my wife - these are her comments: “Wow, this doesn’t even feel as though I have shoes on! They fit everywhere. They are so light weight, too. I need more in other colors!” I think that qualifies as being exactly what she wanted.

title: With more foam, could be perfect 'stylish' city or 'walking' shoe.
text: It is a travesty that in 2019 that women should have to enter the search term 'walking' to find a stylish shoe that doesn't shred, slice, or blister one's ankles. Shoes should be made for walking, including the stylish shoes. I never imagined myself in Sketchers, but these check all the boxes for casual & stylish walking shoes. Good for travel, and great for women whom take public transit or else do a lot of walking during the day. I usually wear a size 9 or 8.5, and ordered a 9 in this shoe. The toe box was a little cramped but the material stretches so this was not a problem by the end of the first day. With a little more foam and a thicker sole they'd be perfect city shoes. Given that they stretch I might try a foam insert. At this price I think they should include a thicker sole, more arch support, and more foam. Though I don't expect them to last long with thin sole, very happy that they are comfortable.

title: Comfortable Flats
text: These are really cute and comfortable. I like to wear my shoes without socks and these allow me to do that comfortably.

title: Comfortable
text: I don’t typically don’t wear flat shoes, but these shoes are comfortable with the memory foam inside.

title: LOVE THEM!
text: I have foot issues and need to wear a shoe with a padded insole. That is why I love my Skechers. These shoes are perfect for work! They are dressier than the other Skechers I have and the padded insole is just what I need. They are so lightweight and comfortable. They fit like a glove for your foot. I bought these in 2 colors, navy and tan, hoping I would like them. So glad I did.

title: A More Dependable Croc Fit Than Some Styles.
text: Great for the price. Room enough for wider feet. I think Crocs in general tend to run a little small lengthwise but since width better than normal fit is ok. My toe is almost hitting though on one foot ( my longer one). Instep strap would be too tight on anyone with a high arch. Comfortable for flatfoots like myself.

title: comfortable!
text: feels great on my feet. Just wide enough to leave a ton on room for my toes, but not as wide as the usual croc. Not the prettiest shoe, but definitely the most comfortable. Will buy again

title: Wear like iron and super comfy
text: I have had these for over nine years and they look new. Excellent for going to the farmers market when the grass is wet. They clean up quickly and easily. Super comfortable. I bought the size six and usually wear a 6 1/2 B.

title: Comfortable. Great for a day at a theme park!
text: I love my croc mary janes. I bought these to replace a pair that had lost all of its tread. These are the BEST option for a day at the theme park because they are super comfortable for walking and transition easily to water rides (there's nothing worse than spending the rest of the day at the park in soggy socks and sneakers!)

title: Narrow
text: These women's Crocs are a huge disappointment. I normally wear the 8 Men's/10 Women's in the traditional/unisex Crocs, and even sizing up to a Women's 11 in this style, the toe box was narrow and short. I hate that Crocs can't seem to make a foot-shaped but feminine shoe for women. I returned these immediately.

title: Very happy!
text: Holy smokes! I ordered these to garden in, but they are so comfortable that I've been wearing them around the house. I wear 8.5 sneakers. I ordered size 9. They stay on no problem.

title: Perfect, pretty feet.
text: Love love my first crocs EVER. so comfy. I wear 8.5 so ordered 8 and they're perfect.

title: Love this Mary jane style!
text: I bought these to replace my old pair I've had for about 15 years! The mary jane style is a favorite for me.

title: Marshmallow Soles!
text: I bought 6 pair of specialty shoes this year trying to find wiggle room for my square feet, and as many insoles to cushion a recent torn Achilles’ tendon, and bursitis. Nothing gave relief for more than 30 minutes. Then I unearthed an eight year old well-worn pair of purple Mary Janes by Crocs, and in spite of the soles having nearly perished from wear and no longer water proof the relief was instant. The closest Crocs model to my old pair was the women’s Karin Klog and it did not disappoint! The arch support is moderate, but the toe room is ample and the sole is soft and cushion-like. The straps can remain forward so they are easily slipped on and off without bending. On the advice of a few reviewers I went up a size from a women’s 9 to a 10. I can walk again!

title: Nice shoes for the price...
text: From wearing them around the house to see how they fit the shoes were quite comfortable and should work well in the summer months.

title: Shoe in Navy runs a size bigger than the same shoe in black?
text: Odd, because I have the exact same shoe in black and white that fit perfectly. But this pair, in navy, are at least a size too large?

title: Too wide for narrow feet
text: I really wanted these to work because in photos they looked a little more streamlined than the usual Crocs which look ridiculous on my chicken legs and are too wide. Alas, the toebox is still too wide for my feet, which cause my feet to slide all the way down towards the toe end and it is just not wearable. Going up a size wouldn't help because there's plenty of room left by the heel where my feet have slid away from.

title: Four Stars

title: Comfortable enough to walk in all day
text: My daughter and I have wide feet and this is absolutely my favorite Crocs. Cuter than the classic style, your foot doesn't swim in them but gives plenty of room. I like that I can put the back part forward so I can slip them on and off easily or wear it normally and they stay on well. We have a lake house and this is my boating shoe but also, I hate walking barefoot in the house and these are comfortable for wearing all day and easily slipping on and off. I also wear any time I go to the beach and I can walk around in these comfortably all day long (I have bad feet and am picky about shoe comfort).

title: Has a narrow heel and loose ankle strap. Ankle injury waiting to happen.

I hate the heels on Danskos, and it's even worse on this type of shoe because there is not a solid back- only a flimsy, loose, ankle strap. Terrible design.

title: A good, comfortable shoe.
text: I definitely like these Women's Karin Clog crocs. I have wide feet and was thankful to find something that had a feminine look in a wide shoe. My regular crocs are the most comfortable shoes I own and have a good arch in them. I'm quite happy with these crocs overall, but do wish they had a better arch like the standard croc.

title: Love these

title: Love the squishyness but upper part that fits over the foot is much too large.
text: Love the squishyness but upper part that fits over the foot is much too large. I bought these to get over a foot injury - and they worked wonderfully for that. Unfortunately their usefulness is limited. The part that fits over the foot is much too large so my feet slide too far forward in them and my toes overhang the end by an inch or more. So, I'm still using them to shuffle around the house but I really can't use the in realworld walking conditions. I've worn them to the store a few times and have ended up badly stubbing my toes due to the over hang. I think I have fairly average women't feet. Not chubby, not skinny, just average. Maybe they need to make a women't version? Perhaps because they are unisex is why they are too large? No clue really but it's unfortunate. I do want to say how truly wonderful the squishyness is. I do recommend them for injured feet. I tripped on the stairs and missed a step coming down extremely hard on my heel. I ended up on crutches for what was essentially traumatic plantar faciatis. Once off the crutches it was so hard to start putting weight on it again. Getting these and the clog version of theses were miracle workers. I was able to walk in norm

title: Seems to be "the real thing"
text: I have some ankle and hip issues, and finding TRULY supportive sneakers to work out in has been a challenge in recent years. I occasionally get sucked into spending 4 times the amount of $$ on sneakers that sound good in reviews, and maybe even feel good at first. But they all seem to break down so quickly - then they become a hazard for me. I always seem to loop back to Puma Tazon. Unfortunately, either the quality has become undependable for this sneaker OR perhaps there are counterfeits around???? I have now ordered two from this link/seller and both are spot on. Seem to be the real thing.... and have that cushy sole on top of the stiff middle shank my joints seem to need. I do size up 1/2 size and put my orthotics in. The two I purchased here from this exact seller/link seem to be perfect. Supportive, fit well, last well. Tags say, "made in Vietnam."

title: Stiff, clunky, hard
text: I am still wearing these for my fitness classes since I can't return them and in hopes that they will soften up and be less stiff. I have the following issues with them: - Imitation leather material is hard and hasn't broken in to conform to my foot; there is no give like with a fabric shoe. Also does not offer ventilation resulting in hot feet. - Outsole is hard and does not offer much cushion; insole has some memory foam but it is a thin layer. I may try insoles to improve the cushioning. - They feel clunky and thick; it seems like my toes/feet can't get a good read on the floor when doing, say, a STEP program.

title: Love them
text: Love these sneakers. They were a little snug width wise at first. I wore them a few times and broke them in and now they are perfect. Very comfortable and I love e the way they look. Can't beat the price either!

title: Plantar fasciitis
text: I used to have a problem with plantar fasciitis. I used to wear New Balance bc those did an amazing job at clearing up that problem, but for some reason I would get a blister on one of my pinky toes. I did some research and it said this was a great shoe for women with flat feet/plantar fasciitis. I DO NOT regret switching! Puma had always been a great brand, and this shoe is great for my feet, and no more blisters!

title: Gel-sole insole cross-trainers for making feet happy
text: My fiance is a nurse and she use to wear very expensive and uncomfortable shoes to work... I bought her a pair of Puma cross-trainers last year, and these are to replace the ones she's been wearing. These Tazon 6 are a much better shoes than her last pair and the fit is perfect. The soft gel-sole insole is very comfortable for her walking on concrete/tile for 12+ hours each shift and she says her feet are very happy :)

title: Really cute, but runs small!
text: 1 size too small. Bought size 10, which is a half size bigger for me, and my toes were at the end. I was able to give them too my mom who wears a size 9. She loves them though.

By day three the ball of my feet ached. The shoe is wider than normal, the toes being ridiculously wide. There's no arch support. There's no tab to keep the tongue in place so it draws back into the shoe. I bought these to workout in, but the fit is so off for me that isn't even a possibility.

title: Great shoes, always a go to!
text: These shoes are great and offer decent arch support. I am on my feet for long hours and work in healthcare. Definitely my favorite shoe to wear no matter what.

I also wondered if it would make my feet too hot as it didn’t seem like a breathable material. Back they went. They are very cute tho but I got them to work out in and knew I would never wear it

title: nice and comfy sneaks

If the answer is "yes" then it's a keeper. These sneakers are a "definitely yes!"

title: Comfortable and a very pretty design !

title: Like walking on clouds

Everything I want in a shoe. Don’t hesitate to buy this. They definitely get better once you break them in.

title: nice!

title: Love these shoes

title: Disappointed

They rub my ankles and I seriously feel like I’m wearing shoes two sizes too big. So I decided I’d just return them but when I took them off I discovered just wearing them around inside for about 20 minutes had caused the lettering on the inside to start peeling. So now they don’t look new anymore and I guess I’m stuck with them. In my experience, Pumas tend to be really fitted but these flop around like clown shoes on me.

title: FIT OUT OF THE BOX...as USUAL! ONE CAVEAT
text: Been wearing Sauconys since my running days, decades ago. I'm now 70 and Saucony still fit me the best even with bunions and I broke a toe that sticks up a little. They have always been wear out of the box shoes for me and give me the support I need. IF I was still a runner, I would upgrade, but for my needs, doing a lot of walking, all day comfort, these are perfect and at a GREAT price. I already have two pairs in different colors, plan on getting a couple more! ONLY CAVEAT: laces are kind of wimpy and I'm going to replace, but that's SO MINOR, not taking a star off. BOTTOMLINE: FIVE STARS for fit, quality, comfort and price.

title: CURRENTLY have FOUR pairs of the Cohesion 11!

title: Lightweight and Comfortable

I use them for walking but I think they would make excellent running shoes as well. Usually I have to buy wide shoes because I have sort of flat feet. title: My favorite shoe

I'm sure they're fine for other less fussy feet. But they're going to the thrift store. I have flare ups after wearing them, there's just no getting around it. I'm writing this review so I don't forget and come back to these in a few years. Self: stick with New Balance.

title: SAFETY ISSUE—PLEASE READ

I love saucony sneakers and have purchased many pairs but this is the first time I have had this issue. I walk on sidewalks near parks and the overflow water from sprinklers is where it is the worst. I even tried scraping the bottom on pavement and it didn’t work well.

title: TR11 Runs small + no arch support
text: I have a narrow foot and high arches. I ordered two models in 7.5 which are both made in Vietnam. The TR13 (which I returned) are cheaply manufactured. The mesh upper is wrinkly and the fit around the foot is very loose even though I ordered the regular width. They're also too big by .5'. The laces are thin and flimsy, they will cut through the islets. The TR11 have better laces and a snugger fit around the foot but they're too small so I'm returning them for a size 8. It's strange that shoes manufactured in the same country would have such a difference in size unless one is a knockoff? Note that the TR11 have zero arch support so I'm going to replace the removable insoles which are flat as a pancake with better ones. Hopefully that will do the trick.

title: The same fit, quality and style as all of our TEVAS at a good price.
text: First time ordering this style of TEVA flips..... We live in the FL Panhandle and we wear flip flops daily. Consequently I have a lot of them, from TEVA’s everyday styles like the mush soles to dressier ones with wedge heels and even some bling. TEVA is by a large margin mine and my family’s favorite brand. The arch support alone is worth what you pay even if they didn’t last for 5+ years! I bought these at the same time as a pair of the mush soles I bought to replace a worn out 5+ yr old pair of the same mush sole flips. I wanted to try this newer style flip as they have a mush insole with a harder exterior sole making them look a bit dressier than my regular mush flips. They seem to be the same excellent quality, fit the same as all my TEVAS, have the same great arch support as my mush flips. These were a bit more expensive than the mush flips but worth the extra cost. At this point, a few weeks after my purchase I would recommend them highly. If that changes for any reason I will post an addendum to this review.

title: comfortable sole, not so comfortable straps
text: these are overall really comfortable flip flops. i wish they came in half sizes since for some reason when it comes to flip flops the sizing is always weird: too small and the straps are too tight or the plug is too low on the sole. too big and the sole it's too large and it feels more like a snow shoe. these however seem ok. i usually wear a 7.5 and got an 8. the straps and plug placement are perfect and the sole it's only slightly oversized. the padding is extremely comfortable. i wear flip flops as house shoes and running errands so i wear them a lot. the sight arch support is very nice, and just enough cushion to be soft but not overly mushy (which my last pair of flip flops were, i keep sliding off them they were so soft) the one downfall of these flip flops are the straps. while they fit great, they are chafing me terribly. whatever material these straps are it's incredibly rough and unforgiving. i am hoping this goes away over time, but I'm already looking for ways to soften the straps so they don't rub my feet raw. until then, anti-chafing cream for me.

title: Not good arch support. If you overpronate, keep looking.
text: I spent hours and hours searching for a pair of flip flops that actually has arch support and is cute. 99% of supportive flip flops look like they are made for my grandma. It blows my mind that we still have not figured out how to make attractive shoes that don't damage our feet for women under 60, but that's a rant for another day... These flip flops have great reviews all over the internet. Everyone loves how comfy they are, and they are comfy. The footbed is nice and squishy. The nylon bands are soft and not the kind that dig into your foot or scrape your skin off. But arch support? Nope. While these aren't completely flat, the arch of the sandal is at least 1/3 inch from my actual foot arch. I have moderately high arches and as a result, overpronate, and these do absolutely nothing to support my foot. So, the search continues. If you want a regular flip flop that doesn't require a break in period, these are great. If you actually want supportive footwear, keep looking.

title: Bottom construction potential safety hazard.
text: Perfect flip flops in the fit. I have long slender feet. What I don't like is the bottom has two bands of a rubbery finish but the rest of the bottom is a felt like product. I know they are making a lot of shoes like this lately, especially Payless shows but if you hit a carpeted or tile area wrong you could potentially slide and hurt yourself. I guess show companies make a lot of extra profit with this construction so it over rides our safety. I would have ordered more pairs of the bottom has a full rubbery finish.

title: Scratchy under strap until I filed it down

Luckily had an adhesive owie strip with me. Used a nail file to smooth it out when I was home. Took a long time, but now I can wear comfortably without getting rubbed raw. Has to do with stitching and how the heat application (instead of a knot or backstitch) wasn’t smoothed enough. Good price, seem well made, and I’ll probably buy again knowing I may have to do some labor. Since the right shoe was fine, maybe it was an anomaly.

These are a neutral looking shoe that he can wear with casual khaki pants. They are very comfortable to wear for extended lengths of time. It seems like most sneaker shoes are either brightly colored these days or plain black or white. It's nice to see an alternative to those.

Those perforated clogs are fantastic—but cold in the winter. These are just as comfortable but unperforated, so warmer. I could do without the fleece edging, but so far it’s not looking ratty (and if people can wear fleecy Uggs to work I don’t see why I can’t wear these!). Even without a back they stay on my feet easily (but also note: if you have trouble keeping clogs on, the trick is to push down with your big toe as you’re starting to lift your foot at the end of the step—it flips the clog’s heel up to meet your heel and they stay on). They are comfortable and they look really nice.

text: I now own a black pair and a white pair. I will be buying the other colors soon. They are cute but more importantly, they are comfortable all day long!

title: 1/2 size down worked for me!
text: I usually wear a 7 1/2 but I ordered a 7. Length wise fits perfectly but a little loose on the top even with the very first buckle notch. They are super cute!

title: Exactly what I was looking for, but a little large
text: It's amazing how difficult it is to find a thonged leather sandal with a simple strap in back (well, one that isn't slathered with bling that belongs in a Florida retirement community, anyway). I don't like plain old flipflops because they won't stay on when running/jumping/etc; I need a strap to hold them in place. And I want them to be sturdy because I'll be clambering down steep paths to get to the beach or whatnot. These do exactly that, with just enough padding in the sole to be comfortable. They don't provide a great deal of support, but I don't expect them to, either. I do wish they came in more colors (I'd probably buy one of each), and I'd rather be able to tighten them a bit more; I have a tendency to slide around a bit in the sandal, which makes it a little bit wobbly on inclines. All in all, though, these are exactly what I wanted, and show off my pedicure beautifully in the summer.

title: Go to
text: This was my first pair of thong sandals that also wrapped a strap around the heel. These are delightful. If you want the comfort and support of sneakers but the look of sandals .. this is it. I can walk all day in them 14k steps. They look good. Great with shorts to maxi dresses .. love them

title: Broken After 1 Month
text: Pros: - Great support (especially if you have wide feet and are looking for a sandal that will give you support). - They're comfortable without being clunky and ugly. Cons: - The straps are cheap. They will break. I wore these occasionally over a 1 month span and while I was walking a strap just broke off and I had no idea what to do. I fell totally in love with these, they were exactly what I wanted but what kind of sandal breaks after 1 month? I'll answer this for you: Not a sandal that is worth $100. I reached out to them and they did not respond. If you buy this you're for sure being ripped off.

title: Best sandal
text: I only buy Vionic shoes and sandals. They are the best if you have arthritic knees and hips. I can walk a lot in these and my legs don't hurt. They are cute on and easy to keep clean.

title: These shoes are awesome!

Yes they’re expensive for such a simple shoe, but if you have plantar fasciitis, and need some cute sandals that go with almost everything, these are it! They’re by far the most stylish comfort sandal I’ve ever had! I’m a bargain shopper so this spend was hard for me, but worth it. My only complaint about this shoe is I wish the color was a little lighter shade.

These fit great :) I have had them for about a year and have gotten a lot of use, so they are definitely durable (something else I have noticed about this brand in general)

title: Not my favorite model by the brand
text: Just recently got into these shoes cause of their crazy comfort and convenience. I live in San Diego so it's summer all year round and the beach is a frequent place we visit. I have picked up a few different styles in the last few weeks shopping deals and sales to help offset the cost, as I was replacing many old boat shoes and canvas shoes. With the 5 different "models" I've chosen the Chiba is my least favorite though I hoped it would be my most. The traction in the bottom of these seems to be a bit superior and less slippery, but the rolled lowered heel feels very strange. It's not easy to get used to and seems like it will create some rub on the back of my heel. They are a LITTLE snug. I wear an 11.5 normally and when these don't have half sizes I go with a 12 and it seems to work after a bit of stretching or even just after putting them on, so these were similar but a smidge smaller, not a deal breaker though. Great shoes, and the rounder and vagabond are my favorite slip on canvas version like these, but these ones will be on the back burner. Got them clearance for 24.99 so I won't return them but not my favorite

title: review for man's sanuk

title: Very comfortable

The back of the shoe that covers the back of your foot above the heel is cut irritatingly low and all but, slips off when you walk. These shoes are ridiculous the way they’re made and an active person can’t wear these. I loved Sanuks long enough and now the manufacturers pull this stunt. These are going back for refund and I will never buy, these online again. You can’t trust the company.

Because they are lightweight, I am not sure that they are well suited for a long day at work if you are on your feet all day. They are casual shoes and look good with jeans. Depending on the workplace, this shoe might be too casual or may not provide enough arch support.
